_note: Sites researched from public pages (mostly Wikipedia infoboxes). verified=false means the coordinate is a proxy or not confirmed: see unverified_reason. Slater Plain is omitted: no coordinate found. Pairs are BODY-LEVEL: sources call the Earth sites Mars or Moon analogs in general; no opened source pairs an Earth site with a named Moon/Mars site. A hit means ANY listed Earth site is found.
hit_rule: A hit = a top-10 Earth match lies within max(site radius_km, 100 km) of ANY Earth site in earth_ids.

sites.name: Atacama Desert (Yungay region, Mars analog)
sites.source_note: Wikipedia gives desert centre 24.5S 69.25W and says the Yungay area is a Mars analog used by NASA to test Mars instruments. NASA page https://astrobiology.nasa.gov/news/nasa-tests-life-detection-drill-in-the-atacama-desert/ confirms Yungay Station drill tests but gives no coordinates.
sites.unverified_reason: Coordinate is the desert centre, not Yungay Station. The McKay 2003 PDF (about 24.08S 69.98W per search snippet) could not be opened. Wikipedia 'Yungay, Chile' is a different town (37S).

sites.name: Mauna Kea (summit; PISCES/Apollo training slopes)

sites.name: Deuteronilus Mensae
sites.source_note: Wikipedia gives 43 54N 337 24 labelled W, about 937 km across. Treated as 337.4E = -22.6 because the USGS map title 'MTM 35337, 40337, 45337' (https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/sim3079) uses east longitude 337.
sites.unverified_reason: Wikipedia's W label conflicts with an east-longitude reading. The USGS map page returned 403 for the extent; the E interpretation is inferred.

pairs.basis: Wikipedia: Haughton, McMurdo Dry Valleys and the Atacama (Yungay) are described as Mars analogs. Atacama coordinate is approximate (desert centre).
Wikipedia/news: Askja and Hawaii slopes were used to train Apollo astronauts; HI-SEAS has a lunar scenario. Mauna Kea coordinate is a proxy.
